confidence_note: Dave Cooper's after-action review and 'I screwed that up' come from a book-notes page; the original text was not readable and sources call him a military team leader without naming his unit in every case, so the story calls him that. Pixar: only 'plussing' and the BrainTrust as candor practices are supported; the old text's quoted Pixar sentences were dropped. The vulnerability loop sequence is given consistently by two summaries.
facts: Dave Cooper's teams hold an after-action review right after each mission.
Enlisted men lead it; there is no rank, no agenda and no minutes.
The team replays each decision and keeps asking why until the truth comes out.
Cooper says the most important words a leader can say are 'I screwed that up.'
Coyle describes a vulnerability loop: A signals vulnerability, B detects it, B signals their own, A detects that, and a norm of trust forms.
At Pixar, teams 'plus' early drafts by offering solutions instead of giving notes.
scene_details: a review held right after the mission, no rank, no agenda, no minutes
tension: A leader's admission, not a speech about openness, is what lets everyone else admit things too.
opening_idea: Open with the after-action review: enlisted men leading it, no rank, no agenda, no minutes.

lessons.idea: When the person with the most standing admits an error first, others find it easier to say what they got wrong, and problems surface sooner.
lessons.anchor: Cooper's 'I screwed that up' opens the review

reflect_final: What is one mistake of yours from this month that you could say out loud to your team in a single sentence?

use_cases.situation: A project finished and nobody wants to say what went wrong
use_cases.move: Start the debrief yourself: 'I screwed up this step; here is what I would do differently.'

use_cases.situation: A colleague shows an unfinished draft
use_cases.move: Add a suggestion to what works, the Pixar way of plussing, instead of listing flaws.

use_cases.situation: Your kid hides a bad grade
use_cases.move: Tell them about a recent mistake of yours first, then ask about theirs.

pocket_idea: Say 'I screwed that up' first, and watch who speaks next.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: After every mission Dave Cooper's teams ran a review with no rank, no agenda and no minutes.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Daniel Coyle describes Dave Cooper's review right after each mission: enlisted men lead it, no rank, no agenda, no minutes, and every decision is replayed with why. Cooper says a leader's most important words are I screwed that up. Coyle calls what follows a vulnerability loop.
